verses.70:2: Inclinai para mim o vosso ouvido, * e salvai-me.
verses.70:3: Sede para mim um Deus protetor, e {munitum}: * para me salvardes,
verses.70:4: Meu Deus, arrancai-me da mão do pecador, * e da mão do que age contra a lei e do iníquo:
verses.70:5: Porque vós sois a minha paciência, Senhor: * Senhor, a minha esperança desde a minha juventude.
verses.70:6: Em vós {confirmatus} desde o seio materno: * desde o ventre da minha mãe vós sois o meu protetor.
verses.70:7: Em vós está sempre o meu {cantatio}: * tornei-me como um prodígio para muitos: e vós sois {adjutor}.
verses.70:8: {repleatur} de louvor, para cantar a vossa glória: * a vossa grandeza o dia todo.
verses.70:9: Não me lanceis fora no tempo da velhice: * quando desfalecer {virtus}, não me abandoneis.
verses.70:10: Porque os meus inimigos {dixerunt}: * e os que {custodiebant} a minha alma {consilium} juntos.
verses.70:11: Dizendo: Deus o abandonou, {persequimini}, † e prendei-o: * porque não há quem {eripiat}.
verses.70:13: Sejam envergonhados, e desfaleçam os que difamam a minha alma: * sejam cobertos de vergonha e de {pudore} os que buscam {malamihi13}.
verses.70:14: Eu, porém, esperarei sempre: * e acrescentarei {adiciam} todo o vosso louvor.
verses.70:15: A minha boca anunciará a vossa justiça: * a vossa salvação o dia todo.
verses.70:16: Porque não {cognovi} {litteraturam}, † entrarei {potentias} do Senhor: * Senhor, eu me lembrarei {solius}.
verses.70:17: Deus, vós me ensinastes desde a minha juventude: * e até agora {pronuntiabo} as vossas maravilhas.
verses.70:18: E até a velhice e {senium}: * Deus, não me abandoneis,
verses.70:18b: Até que eu anuncie o vosso braço * a toda a geração que há de vir:
verses.70:19: {potentiam} e a vossa justiça, Deus, † {altissima}, {magnalia} que fizestes: * Deus, quem é semelhante a vós?
verses.70:20: Quantas tribulações me mostrastes, muitas e más: e, voltando-vos, me {vivificasti}: * e dos abismos da terra de novo me {reduxisti}:
verses.70:21: Multiplicastes a vossa magnificência: * e, voltando-vos, me consolastes.
verses.70:22: Pois também eu, {vasis}, vos darei graças {veritatem}: * Deus, a vós entoarei salmos com a cítara, Santo de Israel.
verses.70:23: Os meus lábios exultarão quando eu vos cantar: * e a minha alma, que resgatastes.
verses.70:24: {sedet} a minha língua meditará a vossa justiça o dia todo: * quando forem envergonhados e desonrados os que buscam {malamihi24}.

decisions.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum
decisions.why: 70:1a is word for word 30:2a and the last line of the Te Deum (glossary formula row; Ps 30 decision `confundar`). Identical Latin gets identical Portuguese (rule 6): Ps 30's ruling is copied with its options — the future of D15's verb, with D23's order for a negated in ætérnum so that the negation is not heard as 'not for ever'. The Greek here too is the optative μὴ καταισχυνθείην (the wish, DRB 'let me never be put to confusion', MS1932 'não permitas que eu seja para sempre confundido'). If Gustavo changes it in Ps 30, it changes here.

options.label: jamais serei envergonhado
options.note: Ps 30's stylist option; drops the phrase of in ætérnum.

options.label: não seja eu envergonhado para sempre

forms.confundar: não seja eu envergonhado para sempre

options.note: The wish (the Greek optative; DRB, MS1932); risks 'not for ever'.

options.label: não serei envergonhado para sempre
options.note: The v1 stylist's native order; D23's 'not for ever' risk.

decisions.why: Copied from Ps 30:2 (decision `libera` there): the natural order, liberáre → livrar. The Latin's order is the Monday Sext antiphon's (from 30:2b), which can be built in its own order.

The one place 70:1 goes beyond 30:2. erípere → libertar where no source is named (row; 6:5, 118:153, 118:170 'libertai-me'); here nothing follows, so 'arrancai-me' would hang. It stands beside líbera me → 'livrai-me' as ῥῦσαί με καὶ ἐξελοῦ με do in the Greek: two verbs, two Portuguese verbs. DRB 'deliver me … and rescue me'; MS1932 'livra-me e põe-me a salvo'.

options.label: libertai-me
options.note: Ruling: the row, no source named.

options.label: arrancai-me
options.note: The row's verb with a source; hangs here.

options.label: ponde-me a salvo
options.note: MS1932's phrase; another verb's meaning, and 'salvo' echoes 70:2 'salvai-me'.

decisions.why: 70:3a is 30:3b with 'in locum munítum' for 'in domum refúgii'; the shared words are copied ('Sede para mim um Deus protetor … para me salvardes'; the 'in' of the Hebraism not reproduced, as Ps 30 ruled). locus munítus → lugar fortificado (row, beside 30:22 and 59:11 'cidade fortificada'); τόπον ὀχυρόν. DRB 'a place of strength'; MS1932 'um asilo seguro'.

decisions.latin: Quóniam firmaméntum meum, * et refúgium meum es tu
decisions.why: The Latin puts 'es tu' last, after the mediant. The natural order names the subject and verb first ('Porque vós sois …'), which is also how 30:4 has the near-identical 'Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu' ('Porque vós sois a minha força e o meu refúgio'). The cost: the second colon is short (5 syllables against 8). The Latin's order is kept as the option; it ends on the oxytone 'vós'.

options.label: Porque vós sois o meu esteio, * e o meu refúgio.

forms.order3b: Porque vós sois o meu {firmamentum}, * e o meu refúgio.

options.label: Porque o meu esteio, * e o meu refúgio sois vós.

forms.order3b: Porque o meu {firmamentum}, * e o meu refúgio sois vós.

decisions.why: D31 names this verse: where God is the firmaméntum of a person, 'esteio' (17:2, 24:14); a blind reader heard 'o meu firmamento' as 'my sky'. στερέωμα.

options.label: firmamento
options.note: The cognate; heard as the sky.

options.label: apoio
options.note: Plainer; a word with no image of the prop.

decisions.latin: In te confirmátus sum ex útero
decisions.why: confirmáre with a person as object → firmar (the row's proposal from 37:3, 40:13, 50:14: 'confirmar' is heard as attesting, or as the sacrament). ἐπεστηρίχθην, 'I was propped upon you'. The passive is the Latin's; MS1932's reflexive 'me firmei' makes it the man's own act. 'In te' → 'Em vós', so that 70:6 and 70:7 keep the Latin's anaphora ('In te … In te'). ex útero → 'desde o seio materno' (row venter/úterus, which names this verse as a near twin of 21:10–11); de ventre matris meæ → 'desde o ventre da minha mãe', word for word 21:11.

options.label: fui firmado
options.note: Ruling: the row, the passive kept.

options.label: fui sustentado
options.note: 36:17's verb (ὑποστηρίζει), close to the Greek here.

decisions.why: cantátio (ὕμνησις), only here in the psalter (grep): the act of singing, a song. 'canto' is the plain noun of 'cantar'; it is carmen's word in 39:4 (ὕμνον there, the same Greek root, so D15's test allows the merge). 'cântico' is cánticum's. The Latin is verbless; the copula is supplied ('está'), and 'Em vós' kept first for the anaphora with 70:6. DRB 'Of thee shall I continually sing' and MS1932 'Tu serás sempre o assunto dos meus cânticos' both explain.

adjútor → auxílio (the row, open for Gustavo; uniform in the psalter, held against the Latinist's 'auxiliador' in 61:7, 118:114, 9:10). No possessive in the Latin: 'um auxílio forte', the copula supplied. βοηθὸς κραταιός. MS1932 'um poderoso protector' (another noun).

options.label: um auxiliador forte
options.note: The agent noun the Latinist asks for elsewhere.

decisions.why: πληρωθήτω — not 62:6's ἐμπλησθείη (→ 'fartar-se', the satiety of food), so 'encher-se', the plain verb. The jussive with 'Que', as the glossary's other jussives (26:14, 62:6). MS1932 'Encha-se a minha boca de louvor'.

options.label: Que a minha boca se encha

forms.repleatur: Que a minha boca se encha

decisions.why: virtus mea, a man's strength failing: 'o meu vigor', as 21:16, 30:11b, 37:11 have it (conc.py). The virtus row's 'poder' is for God's power; 'força' is fortitúdo's. ἰσχύς. The future perfect said as the future subjunctive ('quando desfalecer'), which is how Portuguese says it. defícere → desfalecer (row).

εἶπαν … ἐμοί: 'said to me' or 'said of me'; the speech itself follows in 70:11 ('Dicéntes'). 'falaram de mim' keeps the dative of reference, as 40:6 'dixérunt mala mihi' → 'disseram mal de mim'. DRB and MS1932 both have 'against me', which adds hostility the dative does not say. 'me disseram' leaves the verb without its object until the next verse.

custodíre → guardar (row). Here the guarding is hostile (φυλάσσοντες, watching for a chance; MS1932 'os que insidiavam'), and 'os que guardavam a minha alma' may be heard first as protectors. The Latin word is the same one used of keeping and protecting, and the context ('consílium fecérunt', 70:11 'Deus derelíquit eum') tells which; the irony of guards turned plotters is left open as the Latin leaves it. DRB 'they that watched my soul'.

options.label: guardavam
options.note: Ruling: the row; the context decides, as in the Latin.

options.label: vigiavam
options.note: DRB 'watched'; the hostile watch heard at once; vigiláre's verb.

decisions.why: consílium → conselho for a deliberation (D33); 'fazer conselho' is not Portuguese, 'tomar conselho' is the idiom for deliberating (ἐβουλεύσαντο). in unum → juntos (row; 2:2, 47:5). 30:14's single verb consiliári → 'planejaram' is the option; it loses the noun.

options.label: tomaram conselho
options.note: Ruling: the noun kept, the light verb yields.

decisions.why: The pérsequi row foresaw the rule-3 trap here: bare 'persegui' is also 'I pursued'. D13: with an enclitic object the imperative stands. Portuguese 'perseguir' wants an object, so the pronoun the Latin gives only once ('eum' after comprehéndite) is said with both verbs — grammar (D2); MS1932 has 'persegui-o, e prendei-o' word for word. comprehéndere → prender (row; 7:6, 17:38 after pérsequi).

options.label: ide atrás dele
options.note: Avoids the form entirely; another verb.

decisions.why: The erípere row, no source and no object: 49:22 'e não haja quem liberte' (the Latinist and stylist asked 'livre' there; refused, liberáre's word). Copied here, no object supplied (DRB and MS1932 supply 'him').

elongáre keeps the Latin's 'longe' (row; 21:20 'não ponhais longe de mim', 54:8 'fui para longe'), apart from discédere → afastar-se (37:22 'não vos afasteis de mim'). The row itself proposes 'não fiqueis longe de mim' for this verse (μὴ μακρύνῃς).

decisions.latin: Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice
decisions.why: réspice (πρόσχες) with 'in auxílium meum': 'in' + accusative of purpose, look so as to help. v1 built it as 21:20 ('olhai para a minha defesa'), but 'olhai para o meu auxílio' makes the help the thing looked at (Latinist, stylist; the ambiguity reader heard 'look at my helper'). 'em meu auxílio' is the Portuguese idiom of purpose ('vir em auxílio de'), D40's phrase for 'in adjutórium meum'; the Latin's verb 'olhai' kept. The Hebrew's 'make haste' (DRB) is not the Latin.

options.label: olhai em meu auxílio
options.note: Ruling (v2): the purpose idiom, D40's phrase.

options.label: olhai para o meu auxílio
options.note: v1, as 21:20; heard as looking at the help.

options.label: acudi em meu auxílio
options.note: MS1932 'acode em meu socorro'; another verb.

decisions.why: pudor here is ἐντροπή, the Greek of reveréntia (34:26b 'de vergonha e de desonra') and of verecúndia (D43 joined them by D15's test) → desonra. So 'cobertos de vergonha e de desonra' echoes 34:26b, and 70:24 'envergonhados e desonrados' echoes it within the psalm, as the Greek's αἰσχύνη / ἐντροπή do. confúsio → vergonha (34:26b, 39:16, 43:16); operíre → cobrir (43:16 'me cobriu').

options.label: desonra
options.note: Ruling: D15's Greek test, with reveréntia.

options.label: pudor
options.note: The cognate; today modesty rather than disgrace.

decisions.why: The same colon ends 70:13 and 70:24, one wording in both. quærere → buscar (34:4 'os que buscam a minha alma'); 'mala mihi' → 'males contra mim', as 37:13 'qui inquirébant mala mihi' → 'os que procuravam males contra mim' (the dative of disadvantage). DRB 'that seek my hurt'; MS1932 'os que me procuram males' / 'os que procuram fazer-me mal'. 39:15b's 'os que me querem mal' is for 'volunt', another verb.

decisions.latin: et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam
decisions.why: adícere super → acrescentar a (the row from 60:7, where 'dias sobre os dias' was refused as unidiomatic and 'aos' taken as grammar). 'todo o vosso louvor' is 'all your praise'. MS1932 supplies a noun ('acrescentarei louvor sobre todos os teus louvores').

litteratúra (γραμματεία): writing, the letters, grammar, learning (L&S). 'as letras' keeps the root and holds both senses Portuguese gives it (literacy, and learning — 'homem de letras'); it does not decide between them, as the Latin does not. The Hebrew reads 'numbers' (sephorot), not followed. DRB 'learning'; MS1932 'a ciência (humana)', with a gloss. cognóvi: the perfect of knowing in present sense, 'conheço', as D44 settled at 49:11; the perfect is the option.

options.label: conheci as letras
options.note: The perfect's form (ἔγνων; DRB 'have not known').

decisions.latin: introíbo in poténtias Dómini … Poténtiam tuam
decisions.why: poténtia (δυναστεία) twice in the psalm, plural then singular. It must stay apart from virtus → poder (row; Dóminus virtútum → o Senhor dos poderes, D43) and fortitúdo → força. The Ps 64 draft now in progress has 64:7 'accínctus poténtia' → 'cingido de potência'; followed. 'entrarei nas potências do Senhor' is as strange as the Latin (DRB 'I will enter into the powers of the Lord'); MS1932 paraphrases ('internar-me-ei na consideração das obras do Senhor'). 105:2 'Quis loquétur poténtias Dómini' should copy.

options.label: nas obras poderosas … O vosso poderio

decisions.why: solíus can go with justítiæ ('your justice alone') or with tuæ ('the justice of you alone'); the Greek's μόνου agrees with σου. 'só da vossa justiça' is the plain order; it leans to 'your justice only' (the v2 Latinist), and so does 'somente' at the end; the 'of you alone' reading needs option 3's spelled-out clause. memorári → lembrar-se de (row); proclisis after the vocative with the subject named, avoiding the mesóclise 'lembrar-me-ei' (MS1932).

options.label: da justiça que é só vossa

forms.solius: da justiça que é só vossa

options.note: The Greek's reading; closes the ambiguity.

decisions.latin: et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua
decisions.why: pronuntiáre → pronunciar, as Ps 118:13 and 118:172 have it (no row yet; proposed), kept apart from annuntiáre → anunciar, which the psalm has three times (70:15, 70:18b; D41). The Greek has ἀπαγγελῶ here, the verb of 18b too, so a merge would pass D15's test; kept apart because the Latin's two verbs stand three verses apart. The odd tenses ('até agora … pronunciarei') are the Latin's. mirabília → maravilhas (9:2, 39:6).

options.label: anunciarei
options.note: The Greek's one verb; merges with annuntiáre.

options.label: proclamarei
options.note: The v1 stylist: 'pronunciar' sounds technical. Would change 118:13 and 118:172 with it (new row pronuntiáre, proposed).

decisions.latin: Et usque in senéctam et sénium
decisions.why: Two nouns of age (γήρους καὶ πρεσβείου): senécta, old age, and sénium, 'the feebleness of age, decay' — in use, extreme old age (L&S). v1's 'a decrepitude' was the word's etymological sense, but the stylist heard it as clinical and the ambiguity reader did not know it; 'a idade extrema' keeps the climax the second noun makes (age, then its far end) in plain words. 'os cabelos brancos' (DRB 'grey hairs', MS1932) is the Hebrew's image (seybah), not the Latin's. senéctus (70:9) and senécta both → velhice.

options.label: a decrepitude
options.note: v1: L&S's first sense; clinical, not known to a blind reader.

decisions.why: altíssima, neuter plural (ἕως ὑψίστων): 'even to the highest (places/things)'. 'até as alturas' says the place and keeps the image; the superlative is not heard. excélsa → alturas (D42) is another Latin and Greek word; they do not meet in a psalm. 'até o Altíssimo' would be heard as God's name. MS1932 'que chegam até aos céus' explains; DRB 'even to the highest'.

options.label: até o mais alto
options.note: The superlative kept; the plural goes.

decisions.why: magnália (μεγαλεῖα), 'great things, mighty works' (L&S; ecclesiastical). 'as grandes coisas' (DRB 'great things') keeps it apart from magnitúdo → grandeza (70:8, the same psalm) and mirabília → maravilhas (70:17). The canticle 36:3 'enárrent magnália tua' and 105:21 should copy.

vivificáre → vivificar (row, open; 118:93 'me vivificastes'); two blind readers did not know it, 'dar vida' is the row's option. convérsus → 'voltando-vos' (convértere → voltar), the same in 70:21, where the Latin repeats it.

options.label: destes a vida
options.note: The row's option (MS1932 'deste-me novamente a vida').

decisions.latin: et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me
decisions.why: redúcere: 'lead back' (the Greek ἀνήγαγες is 'led up'; the Latin follows its own verb). v1 'de novo me reconduzistes' kept both íterum and re-, but the stylist heard 'reconduzir' as bureaucratic (reappointing an official) at the close of the psalm's longest verse. 'de novo me trouxestes' says the bringing and the 'again'; íterum carries the return. 'me fizestes voltar' would echo convérsus → voltar in the same verse, falsely. 'tirar' is edúcere's (30:5). DRB 'brought me back again'; MS1932 'outra vez me tiraste'.

options.label: reconduzistes
options.note: v1: the re- kept; bureaucratic in the ear.

options.label: trouxestes de volta
options.note: DRB's build; plainer, 'de novo … de volta' doubled.

options.label: fizestes subir
options.note: The Greek's 'led up'; not the Latin's verb.

decisions.why: vasa (plural) → instrumentos (the row names this verse; 7:14 'instrumentos de morte'). ἐν σκεύει ψαλμοῦ: 'with instruments of the psalm' (DRB 'with the instruments of psaltery'). 'salmo' kept as the Latin's word; the instrument psaltery (psaltérium → saltério) is another word, and the stylist's 'salmodia' is psalmódia's. v2 moves the phrase before the verb (stylist): the colon no longer stacks two prepositional phrases, and 'vos darei graças pela vossa verdade' closes it whole.

confitéri → dar graças a (D5) keeps the dative 'tibi' but cannot take the accusative 'veritátem tuam' as its object; the preposition 'pela' is supplied (MS1932 'pela tua verdade'). DRB keeps the accusative with 'confess'. The verse then has D5's verb as everywhere.

options.label: a vossa verdade
options.note: The accusative kept; 'dar graças a vossa verdade' is not a sentence.

decisions.why: 'Sed et' (ἔτι δὲ καὶ): 'but also, and moreover'. 'Mas também' keeps both particles. The rest is 34:28 ('E a minha língua meditará a vossa justiça'), copied, with 'o dia todo' after the object as 34:28 puts it; 'cum confúsi et revériti fúerint' → 'quando forem envergonhados e desonrados' (D15, the reveréri row; MS1932 the same build).

choices.70:1: = 30:2a + 'e libertai-me'; the Te Deum's last line reads as in Ps 30.
choices.70:2: = 30:3a word for word ('Inclinai para mim o vosso ouvido'); 'et salva me' → 'e salvai-me' (salvum fácere / salváre → salvar).
choices.70:3: = 30:3b except the second place ('um lugar fortificado' for 'uma casa de refúgio'); 'para me salvardes' copied.
choices.70:4: erípere with a source named → arrancar (row). 'do que age contra a lei e do iníquo': two genitives, as DRB reads them; whether one man or two, the Latin leaves open and so does the repeated 'do' only partly.
choices.70:5: patiéntia → paciência (9:19, 61:6: the Latin's word, ὑπομονή, endurance). The Latin's doubled 'Dómine' across the mediant kept; the second colon verbless as the Latin.
choices.70:8: 'a vossa grandeza o dia todo': the object first, as 34:28 'o vosso louvor o dia todo' (D24's 'o dia todo'); 70:15 built the same way. magnitúdo → grandeza (the magnificéntia row keeps grandeza for it); magnificéntia → magnificência in 70:21.
choices.70:9: proícere with no source → 'lançar fora' (16:11 'Lançando-me fora'; the row). derelínquere → abandonar (row; 37:22).
choices.70:11: D13 applied: 'persegui-o' carries an enclitic, so the rule-3 ban does not reach it.
choices.70:13: D15 'Sejam envergonhados'; detráhere + dative → difamar (D39: the row names this verse).
choices.70:19: The objects of 70:18b 'anuncie' continue, as in the Latin (a colon of accusatives with no verb). 'quem é semelhante a vós?' = 34:10.
choices.70:20: 'Quantas … muitas e más': the Latin's pleonasm kept; ostendere → mostrar (59:5).
choices.70:22: psállere → entoar salmos (D25), 'a vós' first as 58:18; cíthara → cítara (row). 'Sanctus Israël' vocative → 'Santo de Israel', no 'ó' (the bare vocative, as elsewhere).
choices.70:23: cum cantávero (future perfect) → 'quando eu vos cantar' (future subjunctive). redímere → resgatar (row; 30:6).
choices.70:24: The first colon = 34:28a with 'Mas também' and 'o dia todo' added; the second = the 34:4 formula in the indicative.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal text for this psalm in the parallels file). 70:1–3 copied from Ps 30:2–4 wherever the Latin is identical (30:2a, 30:3a, 30:3b's shared words); 70:6b from 21:11; 70:24a from 34:28a; 'males contra mim' from 37:13; 'quem é semelhante a vós' from 34:10. Hard readings: 70:16 litteratúram / poténtias / solíus, 70:18 sénium, 70:19 usque in altíssima … magnália, 70:12 in auxílium meum réspice. Rule 3 at 70:11 'persequímini' (the row's foretold trap) met with D13's enclitic. Helper scripts: gl.py (glossary rows by Latin head), conc.py (Latin → current Portuguese across translated psalms).

Hard checks pass. 70:8 'para que eu cante' → 'para cantar' (−2 syllables; the subject is plain from 'a minha boca'). Accepted: the -ai rhyme 70:1/70:2 ('libertai-me' / 'salvai-me'), since both verses copy Ps 30 and the imperatives are the Latin's; length flags on 70:1, 70:2, 70:5, 70:6, 70:7, 70:8 (+4 after the cut), 70:13, 70:18, 70:22, 70:24 (the possessives, articles and supplied copulas Portuguese needs; 70:22b and 70:24b are fixed formulas from 58:18 and 34:4); short colons at 70:3b (the natural order, the Latin's order kept as option), 70:4a, 70:11 (the Latin's 'eum' once; 'e prendei-o' is the whole colon), 70:12b, 70:16a.
No majors, 5 minor. 1 taken (70:12), 4 refused and kept as options or answered by rulings.

outcomes.remark: confúndar as a wish; que eu não seja envergonhado para sempre
outcomes.reason: identical Latin to 30:2, copied with Ps 30's ruling (D15, D23); the wish is option 3.

outcomes.remark: mihi narrowed to 'de mim'; falaram contra mim
outcomes.reason: 70:11 speaks of the psalmist in the third person ('Deus o abandonou'), so the words are about him, not to him; 'contra' adds a hostility the dative does not say (as 40:6 'disseram mal de mim'). Option 2.

outcomes.remark: in auxílium purposive; olhai em meu auxílio
outcomes.reason: with the stylist and the ambiguity reader; D40's phrase.

outcomes.remark: cognóvi perfect; conheci
outcomes.reason: D44: a perfect of knowing in present sense → present. Option 2.

outcomes.remark: veritátem the object, not a cause; vos louvarei … a vossa verdade
outcomes.reason: D5 fixes confitéri → dar graças a; 'pela' is the grammar that verb needs (D2), as MS1932.

audit.note: 8 remarks; best line 70:6, worst 70:22. 4 taken (70:12, 70:18, 70:20, 70:22's order); 4 refused on glossary rows or precedents.

outcomes.remark: fronted 'para sempre'; não serei envergonhado para sempre
outcomes.reason: Ps 30's ruling (D23: after 'não', 'para sempre' is heard as 'not for ever'); identical Latin, identical Portuguese. Option 5.

outcomes.remark: liberte without object; quem o liberte
outcomes.reason: the Latin has no object; 49:22 'não haja quem liberte' copied. Option 2.

outcomes.remark: olhai em meu auxílio
outcomes.reason: as the Latinist.

outcomes.remark: buscar males contra stiff; os que me buscam males
outcomes.reason: 37:13 has 'procuravam males contra mim' for the same 'mala mihi'; one wording kept across psalms. Noted for the glossary.

outcomes.remark: pronunciar technical; proclamarei
outcomes.reason: Ps 118:13, 118:172 already say pronunciar; proposed as a new glossary row (open) with proclamar as its alternative, for Gustavo. Option 4.

outcomes.remark: decrepitude clinical; a idade extrema
outcomes.reason: also an unknown word to the ambiguity reader.

outcomes.remark: reconduzistes bureaucratic and redundant with de novo; de novo me trouxestes
outcomes.reason: íterum carries the return; 'trazer' stays apart from edúcere → tirar.

outcomes.remark: two stacked prepositional phrases; instrument phrase first, 'salmodia'
outcomes.reason: the order taken; 'salmodia' refused (psalmódia's word; psalmus → salmo).

audit.note: 30 readings, 7 unknown words. Acted on 70:12 (fixed) and 'decrepitude' (replaced). The rest are the Latin's own openings or already ruled.

outcomes.remark: persegui-o heard as 'I pursued him'
outcomes.reason: D13: Brazilian speech says 'eu o persegui', so the enclitic marks the imperative; 'e prendei-o' follows at once and 'Dizendo:' frames it as speech.

outcomes.remark: guardavam heard as protectors
outcomes.reason: the Latin's word is the same; the irony is left open as the Latin leaves it.

outcomes.remark: prodígio heard as positive
outcomes.reason: prodígium is equally open (a portent / a marvel); prodígios row (45:9).

outcomes.remark: potências vague; solíus ambiguous
outcomes.reason: the Latin is as strange; for solíus see the decision (option 3 spells out 'of you alone').

outcomes.remark: unknown: esteio, iníquo, vivificastes, magnificência, cítara, potências
outcomes.reason: glossary rows (D31 esteio; vivificar open with 'dar a vida' as option); decrepitude replaced.

audit.note: v2: hard checks pass. New soft flags accepted: 70:12b −5 ('olhai em meu auxílio' is shorter than the Latin's proparoxytone 'réspice' colon; nothing omitted), 70:18a +4 ('a idade extrema'). 70:20b now matches the Latin's length. The 70:1/70:2 -ai rhyme stays (Ps 30 copy).

Draft 2: 70:12 'olhai em meu auxílio'; 70:18 'a idade extrema'; 70:20 'de novo me trouxestes'; 70:22 the instrument phrase before the verb. Refused readings recorded as options (confundar option 5, pronuntiabo option 4). prayed.v1.json keeps draft 1.
Gate on draft 2: 3 minor, no major; all held. The v1 fix at 70:12 passed without remark, as did 70:18, 70:20 and 70:22's order.

outcomes.remark: mihi narrowed; falaram contra mim
outcomes.reason: asked at v1 too; 70:11's third person ('Deus o abandonou') makes the words about him; 'contra' adds hostility. Option 2.

outcomes.remark: 'só da vossa justiça' settles solíus; da vossa justiça somente
outcomes.reason: his wording leans the same way ('justice only'); neither order in Portuguese keeps the 'of you alone' reading audible without spelling it out (option 3). Option 2 for Gustavo.

outcomes.remark: veritátem the object; vos louvarei a vossa verdade
outcomes.reason: asked at v1 too; D5 fixes confitéri → dar graças a, which cannot take the accusative, so 'pela' is grammar (D2).
